Issue is that when you sleep at night, breathing is (ideally) autonomic. I was able to "fake" not having hypoxia in office and in the hospital by breathing through my mouth. Crazy stuff.

Thanks! Same, it's crazy! It really does, right? Like...duh, of course your brain works better when you breathe better. But it's not common to hear about this, so no one thought to treat it this way. My PCP diagnosed me with depression but ultimately that was just a symptom too.

It happened so gradually that it was really hard for me (or anyone else for that matter) to be able to tell me I needed it. Symptoms came to a head this year. Constant exhaustion and fatigue, clinical depression. Unable to function at a high level for more than 1-2 hours / day.
I can completely sympathize here. I am so sorry, I really hope you feel better soon. The last couple of years have been a trial for me as well (all sleep related). Sucks. Sleep is everything.

How many times can you get knocked down? How many ways can your identity be taken away from you, before just giving up completely? After you lose your head, energy, skills, and happiness, who are you, really? I’m trying to hold it together but am really struggling to make sense.
